title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: early July 1986. Grothendieck is formalising 'disjonctions'. A disjunction on a set E is a symmetric relation x|o|y, with a reflexivity condition (next page). Modern equivalent: an orthogonality space in the sense of Dacey, Foulis and Randall, or a graph. To it are attached a polarity A ↦ A^⊥ (written C or co-Vr°) and the associated closure A ↦ A^⊥⊥ (here Vr°_E, read by the transcription as Supp°_E). The closed subsets form a complete ortholattice.

A 'correspondance disjonctive' α_* : E ⇒ E' is given by an underlying map ᾱ : E → P(E') (or a relation). On closed sets it acts by α_*(F) := Vr°_{E'}(ᾱ(F)). It must admit a transpose β_* = ^tα_* : E' ⇒ E with the adjunction property: α_*(x) is orthogonal to y' iff x is orthogonal to β_*(y'). The previous page gives three equivalent conditions, the involution ^t(^tα_*) = α_*, and a bijection Corrdis(E,E') ≅ Corrdis(E',E).

This page:
(1) Formula (***): for every A ⊂ E, α_*(Vr°_E(A)) = Vr°_{E'}(ᾱ(A)). By definition the left side is Vr°_{E'}(ᾱ(Vr°_E(A))). So (***) says the closure of ᾱ applied to the closure of A equals the closure of ᾱ(A). This is a continuity property for the closure operators, i.e. α_* is determined by its values on points and preserves arbitrary joins of closed sets. For true disjunctive correspondences it follows from the adjunction: ᾱ(A)^⊥ = β^{-1}-type set, which is invariant under replacing A by A^⊥⊥.
(2) NB: Grothendieck does not know whether a mere 'quasi-correspondance disjonctive' satisfying (***) must be a disjunctive correspondence. In modern terms: does join-preservation (closure-continuity) imply existence of an orthogonality adjoint? For complete ortholattices, a sup-preserving map f : L → M always has a right adjoint g. Then f^† := ⊥∘g∘⊥ satisfies f(a) ⊥ b ⇔ a ⊥ f^†(b). So at the lattice level the answer is yes. The real issue is the point-level description through ᾱ and the exact definition of 'quasi-correspondence' (not visible here).
(3) Definition by analogy with finite disjunctions, where a correspondence may be a genuine map or the transpose of one. α_* is called an 'application' (adjective uncertain) when its transpose β_* commutes with the complement/orthogonal C. Hence, via De Morgan, β_* also commutes with arbitrary infs. That is the ortholattice analogue of a map being both join- and meet-preserving.

The next page restarts the formalisation from scratch on 10 July. It identifies disjunction structures with simple graphs plus a set E_0 of self-orthogonal points.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The definitional underbrace is consistent with α_*(F) := closure of ᾱ(F).

The open question in the NB is answerable at the level of complete ortholattices: join-preserving maps between complete ortholattices are exactly the ones admitting an orthogonality adjoint f^† = ⊥∘g∘⊥. Whether this settles Grothendieck's question depends on his precise definition of 'quasi-correspondance disjonctive', which is not on this page.

ideas.what: Transposable morphisms between disjunction (orthogonality) spaces, acting on ortho-closed subsets and commuting with closure (formula ***)
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of orthogonality spaces / adjointable maps; sup-preserving maps of complete ortholattices with dagger f^†
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dacey (1968), Foulis–Randall (1970s), D. J. Moore (1995), Heunen–Jacobs (2010)

ideas.what: Question whether closure-compatibility (***) of a quasi-disjunctive correspondence forces it to be disjunctive (i.e. adjointable)
ideas.modern_name: Join-preserving maps between complete ortholattices have orthogonality adjoints
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard Galois-connection / quantale theory (Birkhoff polarities, Erné et al.)

ideas.what: Distinguishing 'maps' among correspondences: those whose transpose commutes with orthocomplement, hence with arbitrary infs
ideas.modern_name: Orthomorphisms / complete ortholattice homomorphisms as special adjointable maps

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck independently developed what is essentially the category of orthogonality spaces (Foulis–Randall/Dacey) with a dagger-like transposition, motivated apparently by combinatorics of 'disjonctions' and graphs rather than quantum logic. Historically interesting, but the mathematics is standard.
missed.quote: je dirai que α_* est une application, ou [...] si ^tα_* = β_* a les propriétés suivantes : il commute à C (donc aux Inf quelconques)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Biographical/historical: it documents Grothendieck working on lattice/orthogonality structures in 1986, a topic where his involvement is unrecorded. It adds no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is a routine development of orthogonality spaces, polarities and adjoint transposition, all well established in the quantum-logic and Galois-connection literature. The open question in the NB is essentially resolved by standard ortholattice adjunction theory. Mildly notable only as unrecorded Grothendieck activity in this area.
transcription_corrections: The operator written 'Supp°_E' looks in the image like 'S~vr°_E' / 'Vr°_E'. It is probably the same 'Vr°' notation as on the previous page ('cos Vr°', 'a-Vr°'), not 'Supp'.
'quasi-conv. disjonction' and 'conv. disjonction' should read 'quasi-corr. disjonctive' / 'corr. disjonctive' (correspondance disjonctive).
'multiplicative [?]' is an uncertain reading of the underlined adjective. It may be another term (e.g. a variant of 'applicative'); illegible.
Top line: 'De plus, l'on a alors, pour A ⊂ E' is correct; the label is '(***)'.
